scenes.headline: Working with Delta
scenes.subtitle: Adding transactions and time travel to your data lake.
scenes.narration: Delta Lake is a storage layer over Parquet that adds ACID transactions, updates, and time travel.

scenes.headline: What Delta adds
items: ACID transactions on top of Parquet files
Updates, deletes, and upserts via MERGE
A transaction log tracks every change
Time travel lets you query older versions
scenes.narration: Delta adds ACID transactions on top of Parquet, enabling updates, deletes, and upserts through MERGE. A transaction log records every change, and time travel lets you query the table as it existed at an earlier version.

scenes.headline: Writing and time-traveling Delta
scenes.narration: We write the DataFrame in Delta format, which records the change in a transaction log. Later we read the table with versionAsOf set to three, time-traveling to an earlier snapshot exactly as it looked at that version.

scenes.headline: Delta vs plain Parquet
scenes.narration: Delta layers ACID transactions, row-level operations, and time travel over Parquet. Plain Parquet gives you immutable files with no transactions and no built-in history, which limits how safely you can update data.

scenes.text: Delta turns a plain file lake into a reliable, updatable lakehouse table.
scenes.narration: In short, Delta turns a plain file-based lake into a reliable, updatable lakehouse table with transactions and history.
